Ranking y first is not dominated because it maximizes my chances of getting into the most valuable school where I have the highest priority. For the second choice, I should rank x because it is the second most valuable school and I have a decent priority (2). Although w is also high in priority, x offers more value. If I don't get into y, my next best chance is x due to its value.

For the third choice, I should rank w. Although it is less valuable than x, my top priority at w gives me a strong chance of acceptance if x rejects me.

Finally, z should be last due to its lower value and my lower priority there.

Therefore, my ranking is based on a balance of maximizing value and leveraging my priority effectively.
